claims.text: A tailored nanohierarchical microstructure in CoCrFeNi will maintain low friction and wear from room temperature to 800 °C.
The starting material is equiatomic CoCrFeNi.
The starting CoCrFeNi has a relatively homogeneous, coarse-grained microstructure without engineered nanoprecipitates.
A combined thermomechanical and thermal treatment can induce the proposed nanohierarchical structure in CoCrFeNi.
The target structure comprises nano-coupled grains, dispersed secondary-phase nanoprecipitates, and spatial composition undulations.
The proposed test regime is sliding in air under a controlled load from approximately 25 °C to 800 °C.
Nanoscale precipitates at grain boundaries and within grains act as low-temperature stress relievers.
The nanohierarchical architecture promotes a dense nanocrystalline glaze layer at high temperature.
At low temperature, nano-coupled grains and nanoprecipitates provide multiple deformation pathways that distribute frictional stress.
At elevated temperature, the glaze layer minimizes adhesive and oxidative wear.
The engineered CoCrFeNi will have a significantly lower coefficient of friction than unmodified CoCrFeNi throughout the temperature range.
The engineered CoCrFeNi will have lower wear rates than unmodified CoCrFeNi throughout the temperature range.
Similar nanohierarchical systems suggest an improvement of up to one order of magnitude in wear resistance.
Standard CoCrFeNi typically has higher friction coefficients and wear rates, with performance deteriorating near 800 °C.
The mechanism is applicable in air under moderate-to-high sliding contact loads between room temperature and 800 °C.
Vacuum or extreme wear conditions may alter the proposed mechanism.
Ni50(AlNbTiV)50 with a nanohierarchical architecture achieved wear rates of approximately 10^-7 to 10^-6 mm3/Nm between room temperature and 800 °C.
The magnitude of improvement in CoCrFeNi may depend on the uniformity and stability of the induced nanohierarchical features.

The hypothesis is falsified if treated samples fail to show statistically significant reductions in both friction coefficient and wear rate across the full temperature range, or if the intended adaptive features are absent after testing.
